title: Problem 1.4
statement_text: Given an oriented matroid $\vec{M}$, decide whether there exists a directed circuit of even size in $\vec{M}$.
context_text: An oriented matroid $\vec{M}$ on ground set $E$ is given by its signed circuits $(C^+,C^-)$ (pairs of disjoint subsets satisfying the oriented matroid axioms); their supports $C^+\cup C^-$ are the circuits of the underlying matroid. A signed circuit is directed if $C^+=\emptyset$ or $C^-=\emptyset$, and its size is $|C^+\cup C^-|$. Every digraph $D$ yields an oriented graphic matroid whose directed circuits are the edge sets of the directed cycles of $D$, so the problem generalizes the even dicycle problem (does a digraph have a directed cycle of even length?), solved in polynomial time by Robertson, Seymour and Thomas and independently McCuaig. A digraph is non-even if some edge set $J$ meets every directed cycle an odd number of times; Seymour and Thomassen showed that recognizing non-even digraphs is polynomially equivalent to the even dicycle problem. The authors define an oriented matroid to be non-even if its underlying matroid is regular and some $J\subseteq E$ meets every directed circuit an odd number of times, and prove that, for oriented regular matroids given by a totally unimodular matrix, detecting an even directed circuit is polynomially equivalent to recognizing non-even oriented matroids (odd directed circuits can be detected in polynomial time). For general oriented matroids accessed through a signed-circuit oracle, no algorithm with polynomially many oracle calls exists, even for graphic ones. The complexity remains open for regular oriented matroids in general; already the case of bond (cographic) matroids, i.e. deciding whether a digraph has a directed bond (minimal directed edge cut) of even size, is open.
